newsitem.title: UK: GEC extends gain as UK eases bid control.
newsitem.headline: GEC extends gain as UK eases bid control.

text.p: General Electric Co Plc built on early gains after the British government released the group from undertaking not to buy Siemens AG's defence units, analysts said.
The stock put on an extra 4p to stand 13-1/2p higher at 373p after the news.

"This is good news because it means that a potential problem on the purchase of Siemens has been removed and it also confirms that the UK is changing its policy on domestic competition, that the UK market is not big enough on its own to sustain competition and today's market is more global," said Lehman Brothers analyst Charles Armitage.
GEC is on the short list of bidders to buy Siemens Plessey, the German engineering group's defence business, which is up for sale.
Analysts said the idea that the UK's decision was in any way linked to the possibility that GEC would be chosen as the buyer for the Siemens was far fetched.
"These should be treated as two completely different things," said another analyst.
